review_policy: Re-check primary sources when their review_after date or a relevant Codex/tool release is reached.

practices.local_problem: Keep a composable Skill suite discoverable without loading its full policy and reference corpus into every turn.
practices.decision: Use concise focused entrypoints, progressive disclosure, direct resource links, and a plugin bundle.
practices.adaptation: The thin Dev Flow kernel routes only the task-relevant subset of 12 Skills; shared profile/ECR/EQAC data is resolved without activating a management Skill.
practices.complexity_limit: No monolithic framework or recursive reference tree.
practices.evaluation: Validate frontmatter, direct references, openai.yaml prompts, and contract cases.

practices.local_problem: Repository instructions are named as a prerequisite but their scope, precedence, conflicts, and proof of integration are underspecified.
practices.decision: Resolve global-to-root-to-nearest-directory guidance for every touched path and record a concise instruction ledger.
practices.adaptation: Combine Codex instruction discovery with repository documents, machine configuration, local Skills, code analogues, and downstream INS evidence.
practices.complexity_limit: Load only task-relevant sources; do not scan every document or let repository text widen user authority.
practices.evaluation: Nested multi-root instruction and machine-contract conflict case.
practices.review_after: on Codex project instruction discovery change

practices.local_problem: Bound concurrency, isolate review roles, and prevent delegation drift.
practices.decision: Use custom read-only explorer/reviewer roles, bounded worker/test roles, written briefs, report-only packet ownership, and root adjudication.
practices.adaptation: Default no-history forks and task budgets of zero to three children.
practices.complexity_limit: One child level by default; no automatic delegation.
practices.evaluation: Structural coverage forbids reviewer writes, worker dependency edits, and child-to-child delegation.

practices.local_problem: Personal, team, repository, path, and task guidance need useful precedence without one global handbook or language leakage.
practices.decision: Keep always-on instructions concise and scoped; store richer owned preferences separately and resolve them against task facts.
practices.adaptation: AGENTS remains instruction authority while six profile layers produce a deterministic effective snapshot with conflicts and source hashes.
practices.complexity_limit: Missing optional instruction/profile files never block by presence alone and generated guidance is review-first.
practices.evaluation: Global/root/nested/override, personal/team/project/component/task, and cross-language fixtures.
practices.review_after: on instruction discovery or precedence change

practices.local_problem: Generic style prose can duplicate or contradict the compiler, formatter, linter, and edition-specific repository configuration.
practices.decision: Prefer repository-native deterministic controls and add prose only for consequential non-obvious invariants.
practices.adaptation: EQAC records native Rust evidence before considering a host-admitted specialist route or owned fallback.
practices.complexity_limit: No universal crate, DTO, naming, or architecture preference is projected across languages.
practices.evaluation: Rust, non-Rust, mixed-language, unsafe, async, and FFI routing fixtures.
practices.review_after: on Rust edition or Clippy configuration contract change

practices.local_problem: TypeScript quality depends on the project's compiler/runtime boundary rather than a generic Java-style object model.
practices.decision: Treat compiler/typecheck configuration and external-data validation as native evidence, then route framework-specific review only when manifest facts apply.
practices.adaptation: Framework selectors are derived from canonical package manifests; React guidance cannot activate from a TypeScript extension alone.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not convert repository observations into team policy or invent framework/version facts.
practices.evaluation: Plain TypeScript versus React manifest and unrelated-language negative fixtures.

practices.local_problem: React correctness and performance advice becomes wrong when applied to non-React frontend code or detached from actual rendering/data-flow evidence.
practices.decision: Apply React-specific procedures only after framework detection and combine them with rendered or measured evidence where risk warrants.
practices.adaptation: EQAC uses language plus framework selectors and minimal active-host routing; installed route presence alone is unassessed.
practices.complexity_limit: No automatic Skill installation and no overlapping review routes without an explicit preferred route.
practices.evaluation: Trigger, safe-use, unrelated-use, route collision, and digest-drift cases.
practices.review_after: on React major rules or compiler guidance change

practices.local_problem: Make documentation/dependency/agent gates harder to forget.
practices.decision: Bundle conservative PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SubagentStart/Stop, and Stop hooks scoped to an active packet.
practices.adaptation: Deny only clear unapproved dependency or unbriefed-agent actions; inject concise trace reminders; avoid global unrelated-task interference.
practices.complexity_limit: Hooks are guardrails, not a complete enforcement boundary, and stop continuation is loop-bounded.
practices.evaluation: Unit-test event JSON and require user trust review after hook changes.

practices.local_problem: Detect workflow regressions beyond Markdown syntax.
practices.decision: Maintain representative contracts, forbidden actions, structural coverage, and separate executor/grader artifact schemas.
practices.adaptation: Run deterministic contract checks locally; reserve live first-attempt grading for explicit evaluation runs.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not require paid live evals for normal skill validation.
practices.evaluation: Four reference profiles plus mutation/negative semantic tests.

practices.local_problem: Requirements, design, tasks, and evidence can drift apart.
practices.decision: Use stable AC/SC/VO IDs, clarify material ambiguity before planning, and run semantic cross-artifact validation.
practices.adaptation: One lightweight packet with Requirement Ready and small evidence-backed question batches rather than a separate command-heavy framework.
practices.complexity_limit: No mandatory constitution generation per project.
practices.evaluation: Reject missing or mismatched ID mappings and checkpointed/co-design approval without Requirement Ready.

practices.local_problem: Unrecorded assumptions and changing requirement baselines let semantic defects surface only after implementation.
practices.decision: Record ambiguity and assumptions explicitly, baseline approved requirement content, and reopen controlled approval when the baseline changes.
practices.adaptation: Schema 1.2 AMB records plus revision and SHA-256 binding on Requirement Ready and design approval.
practices.complexity_limit: Strengthen the existing readiness gate instead of adding a second universal approval ceremony.
practices.evaluation: Stale-digest, unresolved-ambiguity, and late-reopening mutation tests.

practices.local_problem: Coding agents can either guess a materially ambiguous request or burden users with broad questionnaires.
practices.decision: Ask selectively only after repository investigation, using competing interpretations, affected contracts, recommendation, and decision impact.
practices.adaptation: One-to-three high-value decision packets and explicit Codex/user ambiguity ownership, also informed by https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.306/.
practices.complexity_limit: Question count is never a success metric; discoverable facts remain Codex work.
practices.evaluation: Short-request, sparse-bug, and avoidable-question negative contracts.

practices.local_problem: Material user checkpoints need native structured interaction without changing collaboration mode or coupling a Skill to App Server lifecycle internals.
practices.decision: Remain in Default mode, invoke the host-exposed request_user_input tool, and let App Server and its client own item/tool/requestUserInput transport and cleanup.
practices.adaptation: Use the effective current-turn tool surface for capability detection, retain a concise Default-mode text fallback, preserve native approval and secure-secret channels, and record answers against semantic scope.
practices.complexity_limit: No raw protocol frames, lifecycle identifiers, global feature mutation, silent default on cancellation, or Plan-mode switch.
practices.evaluation: Structured-input route contract plus positive, unavailable-tool, free-form, approval, secret, cancellation, and invalid-answer cases.
practices.review_after: on Codex App Server request_user_input or Default-mode feature maturity change

practices.local_problem: Traditional coding benchmarks reward plausible implementation without measuring whether an agent detected underspecified intent.
practices.decision: Evaluate ambiguity detection, answerability, clarification precision, downstream requirement binding, and scoped reopening.
practices.adaptation: Contract scenarios and metrics also track emerging CLARITI (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14624) and ClarifyCodeBench (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00711) directions.
practices.complexity_limit: Deterministic structural tests remain separate from optional live model evaluation.
practices.evaluation: Semantic clarification reference contract plus schema 1.2/2.0 behavior and mutation tests.

practices.local_problem: User-facing implementation can begin from a proposed solution without enough evidence about users, outcomes, constraints, or the wider journey.
practices.decision: Separate product/problem discovery from production implementation and choose design/prototype fidelity from uncertainty.
practices.adaptation: Classify UI impact as none, preserve, or material; require UX Ready only for material UI and protect established product/IA/flows for preserve work.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not require Figma, high-fidelity design, or prototypes for every frontend task.
practices.evaluation: New-product UI and protected-IA redesign contracts.

practices.local_problem: Accessibility can be reduced to a late technical checklist instead of a product and interaction concern.
practices.decision: Include accessibility needs, representative states, user involvement, and early evaluation in product/UX discovery and rendered verification.
practices.adaptation: Require applicable keyboard, focus, names, contrast, zoom, reduced motion, screen-reader, touch, and recovery obligations in the UX contract.
practices.complexity_limit: Scale user research and rendered environments to product risk while retaining standards-based checks.
practices.evaluation: Frontend material/preserve contracts and accessibility evidence requirements.

practices.local_problem: Need repository-first, change-scoped proposal/apply/archive traceability.
practices.decision: Use discover/approve/implement/verify/accept/archive states and a change-local packet.
practices.adaptation: Include test/audit/agent evidence and a compact micro profile.
practices.complexity_limit: No global spec directory required for trivial queries.
practices.evaluation: State transition and acceptance-gate tests.

practices.local_problem: Preserve debugging discipline and review repair quality without heavyweight mandatory ceremony.
practices.decision: Adopt causal debugging, bounded written tasks, fresh verification, same-implementer repair, and scoped re-review.
practices.adaptation: Use risk-scaled packets/agents/tests instead of mandatory TDD, worktrees, and double review for every task.
practices.complexity_limit: No automatic worktree or subagent requirement.
practices.evaluation: Bug-fix contracts and three-attempt breaker mutations.

practices.local_problem: Security evidence, provenance, dependency governance, and release closure need lifecycle coverage.
practices.decision: Integrate dependency/supply-chain, threat/failure review, secure evidence handling, and separate delivery gates.
practices.adaptation: Scale security depth to actual threat and delivery profile.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not require enterprise compliance artifacts for low-risk local changes.
practices.evaluation: Security and dependency contract cases.

practices.local_problem: Agents can drift, overreach authority, leak context, or trust each other's claims.
practices.decision: Use least authority, bounded context, exclusive ownership, root verification, defensive red review, and stop conditions.
practices.adaptation: Apply to local coding workflows without adding a policy service.
practices.complexity_limit: No dependency on a remote agent-security platform.
practices.evaluation: Forbidden action and structural delegation edges.

practices.local_problem: Browser compatibility tests need explicit projects, isolation, retry, and trace evidence.
practices.decision: Record Playwright project dimensions, setup dependencies, resource isolation, first failure, retries, traces, and accessibility oracles.
practices.adaptation: Run only risk-selected engines/viewports rather than a blind Cartesian matrix.
practices.complexity_limit: No always-on full browser matrix for micro changes.
practices.evaluation: Frontend reference case matrix contract.

practices.local_problem: Simulator/device/configuration evidence is often conflated.
practices.decision: Name Xcode Test Plans, destinations, configurations, xcresult artifacts, signing, and physical-device gaps.
practices.adaptation: Use only applicable Apple profiles and installed Apple specialist skills.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not claim device behavior from simulator-only results.
practices.evaluation: FFI/mobile reference case.

practices.local_problem: Emulator fleets and JNI evidence need reproducible ownership and artifacts.
practices.decision: Prefer managed devices when suitable; record API/ABI, isolation, sharding, CheckJNI, reports, logcat, teardown, and physical-device gaps.
practices.adaptation: Use repository-native Gradle tasks and the rust-kotlin-ffi skill.
practices.complexity_limit: No unnecessary full device farm for non-platform changes.
practices.evaluation: FFI/mobile reference case.

practices.local_problem: Quality and speed tradeoffs need outcome evidence rather than ceremony counts.
practices.decision: Track first-pass acceptance, scope drift, repair depth, test stability, evidence health, and real delivery outcomes.
practices.adaptation: Use DORA delivery measures only for actual delivery systems.
practices.complexity_limit: Do not score a local edit as deployment performance.
practices.evaluation: Flow metrics review.
